source.author: verg
source.text: Sive errore viae seu tempestatibus acti, qualia multa mari nautae patiuntur in alto, fluminis intrastis ripas portuque sedetis, ne fugite hospitium neve ignorate Latinos Saturni gentem, haud vinclo nec legibus aequam, sponte sua veterisque dei se more tenentem.
source.text_original: Sive errore viae seu tempestatibus acti, / qualia multa mari nautae patiuntur in alto, / fluminis intrastis ripas portuque sedetis, / ne fugite hospitium neve ignorate Latinos / Saturni gentem, haud vinclo nec legibus aequam, / sponte sua veterisque dei se more tenentem.
source.text_english: Whether driven in by a mistake in your route or by storms, as many things sailors suffer at sea in the deep, you have entered the banks of a river and are seated in a harbor; do not flee from hospitality, and do not be unaware of the Latins, the race of Saturn, not fair by constraint or by laws, but holding themselves of their own free will and by the custom of the ancient god.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: Prima deum magnis canimus freta pervia natis fatidicamque ratem, Scythici quae Phasidis oras ausa sequi mediosque inter iuga concita cursus rumpere flammifero tandem consedit Olympo.
reuse.text_original: Prima deum magnis canimus freta pervia natis / fatidicamque ratem, Scythici quae Phasidis oras / ausa sequi mediosque inter iuga concita cursus / rumpere flammifero tandem consedit Olympo.
reuse.text_english: First we sing of the sea passages made traversable by the great sons of the gods, and of the prophetic ship, which, daring to follow the Scythian shores of Phasis and, driven on, to break through its course amid the middle mountain ridges, at last settled on fiery Olympus.
